fields.recommendation: Swap to the zero-lag correlation, which the same panel prints to six decimals and which depends on the synthetic.
fields.evidence: Correlation of a trace with its own exact shifted copy is 1 by construction, and the panel note says so ('why the correlation reaches exactly 1'); a learner who reads the prompt knows it without running anything.

rekey.label: Correlation at zero lag, before any shift

rekey_annot.evidence: suggestBulkShift(s25 synthetic, the 25 Hz synthetic delayed 4 samples, dt 2 ms, max 40 ms) series entry at lag 0: 0.6217418028775199 (computeIntermediate().corrZeroLag, pinned in shiftLab.test.js); prints 0.621742, miss 2e-7. Nearest scan neighbours 0.771383 (lag 2 or 14) and 0.892968 are far outside tol; 1 (the winning lag) fails by 0.378; the SVG label prints it at 4 dp (0.6217, miss 4e-5, passes as it should). Not guessable: continuous.

fields.evidence: 'Tuning thickness' String(model.tuneMs) = 16 on a 2 ms grid; genuinely integer, tol 0 honest.
fields.notes: Derivable without the panel: the prompt's own formula gives 15.59 ms and the measured value is the next 2 ms grid step up (the panel prints the grid overshoot). Also the default panel state (probe).
Identical to tune40_amp (tuning amplitude of an equal and opposite pair is frequency independent on this grid), so one reading answers both fields.

fields.evidence: At 40 Hz the tile reads 10; integer, tol 0.
fields.notes: Same derivability: sqrt(6)/(2 pi 40) = 9.75 ms, next 2 ms step 10.

rekey.label: Amplitude of a 6 ms bed at 40 Hz

rekey_annot.evidence: computeWedge(40).rows[3] (6 ms) amp = 0.09535394608974457 (engine tuningCurve, pinned in wedgeLab.test.js); prints 0.0953539461. Neighbours at 40 Hz: 4 ms 0.0718218, 8 ms 0.1097387, 14 ms 0.0987969, 16 ms 0.0899487; 25 Hz at 6 ms 0.0682633; 50 Hz at 4 ms 0.0837294; tune25_amp 0.1155948, isolated 0.0800000: nearest is 14 ms at 40 Hz, 0.0034 away, all fail at tol 0.0005. By the f x T law 20 Hz at 12 ms prints the same number (240 Hz ms), which is physics and still a reading. Default state (25 Hz, 16 ms) prints the tuning amplitude, never this value.
